# RFC-0011: Portable authorship and attached collaboration records

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** test
> **Owners:** @govctl-org

---

## 1. Summary

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0011:C-SCOPE] Governance authority and attached records (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-scope"></a>

RFC, ADR and Work Item MUST support native creator attribution and attached collaboration history. Comments, review decisions, authorship confirmations and their resolution relationships are attached records, not new governed task artifacts. Runtime scheduling, model credentials, participant authentication and process monitoring remain responsibilities of clients such as Lattice. This RFC extends the artifact definitions in RFC-0000 and the command architecture in RFC-0002.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-ACTOR] Stable actor identity and attribution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-actor"></a>

An actor MUST have a nonempty stable subjectId and display name; optional kind distinguishes human and agent. Existing participantId, agentId, role and roles fields MAY be retained for client interoperability. Names, model identifiers and RFC owners MUST NOT define identity. RFC/ADR/WI MAY carry optional created_by metadata containing this actor, supplied explicitly by actor context on creation. Existing artifacts lacking it remain unknown. Authorship and contributions MUST be bound to specific content revisions; assignment, review and lifecycle-only actions MUST NOT by themselves assert content authorship. Creator declaration and verified authorship MUST remain distinguishable.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-STORAGE] Append-only portable storage (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-storage"></a>

Attached events MUST be stored under gov/collaboration/<kind>/<artifactId>/<eventId>.json for kind rfc, adr or work. Files MUST be published atomically without overwriting another event. Reads and writes MUST reject traversal, symbolic-link escapes, malformed or oversized content and mismatched file/target identities. A repeated idempotent event with identical request identity MUST replay; reuse for different content MUST fail. No repository credential or private signing key may be introduced by these commands.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-TARGET] Exact revision targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-target"></a>

A target MUST identify repoId, kind, id, optional version, contentDigest and optional code commit. For compatibility the document digest MUST be SHA-256 of the compact JSON array of manifest entries with ordered path and sha256 fields, sorted by relative POSIX path. RFC manifests include rfc.toml and its referenced clause TOML files; ADR/WI manifests include their source TOML file. Attached events MUST be excluded. Reads MUST reject source changes during snapshot capture. Append MUST require the current target unless an explicit stale-history operation preserves an older target. It MUST NOT rebind an old review to new content.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-REVIEW] Comments review state and resolution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-review"></a>

Native comments and reviews MUST record their actor, creation time, target and body. Reviews MUST distinguish approved, changes_requested and comment. Replies and explicit resolution records MUST refer to existing records of the same artifact. Query projection MUST distinguish current, stale, resolved and unverified conclusions, creator declaration and confirmed authorship, and independent approvals from self-review. Unknown authors MUST NOT permit an effective independent approval. An unresolved trusted changes_requested remains blocking until explicitly resolved. Approval MUST NOT advance an artifact lifecycle automatically. Clients MAY apply stricter live membership policy.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-TRUST] Declared identity and explicit trust (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-trust"></a>

An unsigned native actor declaration MUST remain visibly declared and MUST NOT count as trusted approval or confirmed authorship. Signed records MUST use an explicitly identified Ed25519 signing key and canonical JSON payload. Verification of cryptographic integrity MUST remain distinct from trust in the signer. A key embedded in a repository event MUST NOT make itself trusted. Clients MAY supply trusted public key files explicitly; private key files MAY be supplied locally for native signing but MUST never enter records or output. Invalid signatures MUST fail append and MUST be reported by validation.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-COMPATIBILITY] Legacy Lattice compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-compatibility"></a>

Native readers MUST accept existing Lattice formatVersion 1 envelopes including review, authorship, resolution, execution, legacy-import, review-assignment and review-run. They MUST preserve original files, IDs, actors, timestamps, targets and signatures without rewriting or implicit re-signing. New native declarations MAY use formatVersion 2 with a null signature. Imports and replay MUST preserve existing bytes. Existing schema-5 RFC/ADR/WI without created_by MUST remain valid; no attribution may be inferred from Git configuration or responsibility metadata.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-CLI] Native collaboration protocol (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-cli"></a>

The collab namespace MUST expose capability discovery, target, list and append operations with machine-readable JSON output. Target/list/append MUST accept explicit repository identity. List MUST support a whole-project batch so clients need not spawn one process per artifact. Append MUST accept a bounded envelope through stdin. Native add MUST support comment, review, authorship and resolution with explicit actor/payload input and a stable idempotency key; local optional signing and explicit target input are permitted. Structured creation and edit actor context MUST be available to native clients. govctl check MUST validate stored collaboration structure and signature integrity without treating unknown keys as trusted. Queries MUST be useful independently of Lattice.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0011:C-ACCEPTANCE] Verification and compatibility evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0011c-acceptance"></a>

Acceptance MUST cover native creation for all three kinds with explicit Agent identity, version-bound contributions, comments and replies, review verdicts and resolution, unsigned versus trusted provenance, content changes, independent review rules, malformed input, traversal/symlink rejection and concurrent idempotent publication. A legacy Lattice signed review MUST verify with its explicit public key and retain exact bytes, target and ID through native reads and replay. CLI contract, schema and generated documentation MUST remain coherent.

*Since: v0.1.0*
